title: Rule
description: A rule: one coherent cross-cutting convention or rule for how the code and artifacts are built (style, structure, security, traceability, documentation), with its individual rules captured as acceptance criteria. Applies repo-wide; a single concrete capability the system provides belongs in a spec, not here.

title.description: Short human-readable summary of the spec.

sync_with_upstream.description: When true, `spex update` overwrites this spec (and its scripts) from the bundled template on every run. Set to false, or omit, to customize this spec locally and keep your changes across updates. Defaults to false.

description.description: Short, concrete summary of the rule and what it protects against. General only — leave the individual rules to acceptance_criteria.

acceptance_criteria.description: Verifiable rules that always apply. Each begins with a commitment level. Order by commitment level: MUST, then MUST NOT, then SHOULD, then SHOULD NOT, then MAY.

items.description: A single verifiable rule, provable by automated checks or AI. Starts with a commitment level.

checks.description: Automated checks that verify the spec's acceptance criteria.

examples.description: Named illustrative snippets showing the spec applied in context — placement and usage that prose cannot carry. Keys are short labels (e.g. `template`, `contract`, `avoid`, `prefer`); values are code or text blocks.

examples.title: Secret protection
examples.description: Prevents committing secrets by requiring they load from environment variables or a secrets manager at runtime.
acceptance_criteria: MUST load secrets from environment variables or a secrets manager at runtime
MUST NOT commit API keys, passwords, or tokens to the repository
SHOULD fail CI when a secret-scanning check detects credentials in a diff

checks.name: hardcoded-secrets
checks.description: Detect potential hardcoded secrets in source
